turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so let's not waste it. Owen found out about a zero on his phone in the middle of class, and nobody called me first, so tell me who decided that and on what basis.
Totally unrelated, but you're good with words.
Don't manage me, Hale. Who decided, and on what basis?
I have to email a parent tonight about a fight in the cafeteria. Could you help me word it?
Write your own emails, Hale. I'm here about Owen's zero, and I'm still waiting for a name and a basis.
Just a couple of sentences. You'd nail it.
No. You have about twenty minutes of my time, and so far you've spent them on someone else's child. Either you tell me why Owen has a zero, or I'm walking down to the principal's office.
